deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. Folio 3r set up two tools. (1) The Lagrange series. (2) For x = z/X with X = 1 + a x^m + b x^{2m} + ..., the coefficient of z^{n+km} in x^n equals n/(n+km) times the coefficient of x^{km} in X^{-n-km}. Folio 3v adds two more general statements and then a worked example.

§3. Let X = 1 + a x + b x^2 + c x^3 + ... . Write X^n = sum_j C(n,j) (X-1)^j. Then
[x^k] X^n = n·[x^k](X-1) + n(n-1)/2·[x^k](X-1)^2 + n(n-1)(n-2)/6·[x^k](X-1)^3 + ... .
Gauss's symbols (gothic letters with superscript k, followed by a, b, c) are read here as 'coefficient of x^k in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd ... power of (X-1)'. This reading is mine. It is confirmed by how the formula is used below. This is simply the binomial theorem applied to 1 + (X-1).

§4. Let x = z/X, with X = 1 + a x^m + b x^{2m} + ... .
- Then log x = log z + A z^m + B z^{2m} + C z^{3m} + ... .
- The coefficients are [z^{km}] log x = (1/km)·[x^{km}] X^{-km}.

Proof (mine), by Lagrange–Bürmann. Put φ = 1/X, so x = zφ(x) and log x − log z = log φ(x). Then
[z^N] log φ(x(z)) = (1/N)[w^{N-1}] φ'φ^{N-1} = (1/N^2)[w^{N-1}](φ^N)' = (1/N)[w^N] φ^N.
This is exactly Gauss's formula with N = km. It is the n→0 limit of item 2 on the previous page.

§5. Example. X = 1 + x^4/10 + x^8/24 + 5x^12/208 + 35x^16/2176 + 3x^20/256 + ... .
- The general coefficient is (1·3···(2k−1))/(2·4···2k)/(4k+1). The marginal note 1.3.5.7.9/2.4.6.8.10 gives 63/256, and 63/256 ÷ 21 = 3/256.
- Hence xX = ∫_0^x dt/√(1−t^4), so z = xX is the lemniscatic integral.
- Therefore x = sl z, the lemniscatic sine. The page computes the power series of log(sl z / z) through z^16. The next page continues to z^20.

With m = 4, each coefficient is (1/4k)[x^{4k}] X^{-4k}, expanded by §3 with n = −4k.

k=1: (1/4)(−4·1/10) = −1/10.

k=2 (n = −8): (1/8)[−8·(1/24) + 36·(1/10)^2] = (1/8)(−1/3 + 9/25) = (1/8)(2/75) = 1/300.

k=3 (n = −12):
- First power: −12·5/208 = −60/208 = −15/52.
- Second power: +C(−12,2)·2·(1/10)(1/24) = 78·2/240 = 156/240 = 13/20.
- Third power: C(−12,3)·(1/10)^3 = −364/1000 = −91/250.
- Sum: (−1875 + 4225 − 2366)/6500 = −16/6500 = −4/1625.
- Times 1/12 gives −1/4875 (scratch figures 1456, 39000, 25446 − 25350 = 96, etc.).

k=4 (n = −16): (1/16)[−16·35/2176 + 136·(2·(1/10)(5/208) + (1/24)^2) − 816·3·(1/10)^2(1/24) + 3876·(1/10)^4].
- These are Gauss's terms −16·35/2176 + 136/208 + 136/576 − 16·51/800 + 16·17·18·19/(24·10000).
- They reduce to −35/136 + 17/26 + 17/72 − 51/50 + 969/2500.
- Grouping −35/136 + 17/72 = (−315 + 289)/1224 = −13/612.
- Grouping 17/26 − 51/50 = (425 − 663)/650 = −119/325.
- Then −119/325 + 969/2500 = (−11900 + 12597)/32500 = 697/32500.
- Finally 697/32500 − 13/612 = (106641 − 105625)/4972500 = 1016/4972500 = 254/1243125.
- Times 1/16 gives 127/(325·25·153·8) = 127/9945000.

Result: log sl z = log z − z^4/10 + z^8/300 − z^12/4875 + 127 z^16/9945000 − ... .

Marginal fractions 1/30, 4/65, 127/2040 are the successive ratios of consecutive coefficients: (1/300)/(1/10), (1/4875)/(1/300), (127/9945000)/(1/4875). Next page: 127/(65000·153) = 127/9945000, then the z^20 term.
errors: No substantive errors. Every reduction checks out: 1/300, −1/4875, and 127/9945000 are all confirmed by direct computation from sl z = z − z^5/10 + z^9/120 − 11z^13/15600 + ... .

The term written (as transcribed) −57/50 must be −51/50, since 16·51/800 = 51/50. Gauss's subsequent step 663 = 51·13 shows he used 51. This is either a misreading of the digit or a harmless pen slip.
The notation in §3 is compressed and not self-explanatory. The superscripted gothic letters must be read as coefficients of x^k in successive powers of (X−1). The usage confirms this reading.

results.what: Coefficient of x^k in X^n via binomial expansion of (1+(X−1))^n
results.modern_name: binomial/multinomial coefficient extraction (power of a power series)
results.usually_credited_to: standard (Newton; Euler, Arbogast for power-series powers)

results.what: For x = z/X(x): [z^{N}] log x = (1/N)[x^N] X^{-N}
results.modern_name: Lagrange–Bürmann inversion formula applied to H = log

results.what: Power series of log(sl z / z) for the lemniscatic sine, via inversion of z = ∫_0^x dt/√(1−t^4): −z^4/10 + z^8/300 − z^12/4875 + 127 z^16/9945000 − ...
results.modern_name: Taylor expansion of log of the lemniscatic sine (inversion of the lemniscatic integral)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss's lemniscatic investigations (1797–98); series of sl studied by Gauss, later Abel/Eisenstein

deep.surprise_reason: This is Gauss's well-documented 1797–98 work on inverting the lemniscatic integral by series. It uses Lagrange inversion, which was standard. The explicit log-series coefficients are an unpublished computational detail but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: '−57/50' should read −51/50, since 16·51/800 = 51/50 and 663 = 51·13 is used next.
The struck marginal '127/3040' is the ratio of consecutive coefficients and should be 127/2040, since (127/9945000)/(1/4875) = 127/2040.
'36(1/100)' is 36·(1/10)^2 = C(−8,2)·a^2; the overwritten '30' is irrelevant.
The next page's '1/4975 z^12' should be 1/4875, as computed on this page.
